html:
The cashew tree, brought to West Africa from Brazil by the Portuguese, became the main cash crop of Guinea-Bissau from the 1980s, when farmers planted it widely.

Today Guinea-Bissau is one of the largest cashew producers in Africa, and raw nuts are the great bulk of its exports, most shipped from Bissau for shelling in India and Vietnam. Many farmers swap nuts for imported rice, and a poor season or a low price means hunger. Dependence on one crop leaves the state and its people exposed. The tree also spread across Ivory Coast, now the world's largest grower, and other West African countries. See also Portuguese Guinea.
sum: The cashew tree, brought to West Africa from Brazil by the Portuguese, became the main cash crop of Guinea-Bissau from the 1980s, when farmers planted it widely.
